title: QL-1.01 Red-team gate: no contract is signed without a clean record that matches its spec
request: Closes quality-loop principle 1 (red-team each contract before signing) and the signing-time part of principle 2 (red-green primary, document-only checks never count toward done). A zero-dependency node script reads a contract spec and its red-team record and reports SIGNABLE, NOT SIGNABLE with reasons, or NO RECORD; a test proves every refusal rule; the seed-gate and the sign runbook call it. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-0.03.

tasks.title: The gate script and its refusal rules
requirements: scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs takes spec paths (default: every file under contracts/seed-readiness/specs/ and contracts/quality-loop/specs/) and prints one line per spec: SIGNABLE, NOT SIGNABLE: <reasons>, or NO RECORD; exit 0 only when every named spec is SIGNABLE; --report mode exits 0 unless a record is malformed, a hash mismatch is claimed clean, or a signed contract under contracts/signed/ has a spec without a SIGNABLE record

the record is contracts/<area>/redteam/<id>.json with schema memev-redteam/1 and snapshots <id>.r<n>.spec.json beside it; spec_sha256 is sha256 of the spec as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, workdir null)

SIGNABLE requires all of: record parses with the schema and the spec id; rounds numbered 1..n without gaps; the last round has verdict clean and an empty answers list; its spec_sha256 equals the spec on disk; every answer in every round has disposition added or rejected; every added criterion is present verbatim (task, statement, verifier type) in the spec on disk; every rejected answer has a non-empty reason; the sequence of snapshots never weakens (no task or criterion removed, no verifier type changed, no metric loosened, no command changed except as recorded in an amendments list the round names, no scope glob added or broadened); every implement task has at least one test_red_green criterion unless the spec's manifest row declares kind docs or evidence; every input file of the clean round whose blob at HEAD differs is reported, and under src/ it is NOT SIGNABLE
node 23 compatible, no dependencies, first lines carry // gate-version: 1 and the SPDX header

each round is a DSSE envelope signed by a reviewer key that is not a contract-signing key (not under contracts/keys/); the gate holds the reviewer public keys it accepts and refuses an unsigned round, a round signed by another key, and any edit to an earlier round, snapshot or disposition after a later round was signed. Honest limit, stated in docs/CONTRACTS.md: while the builder and reviewer run as one user on one machine the reviewer key is readable by both, so the signature makes tampering visible in history but is not separation; separation comes from a reviewer key the owner holds off the build machine or from the second human of SR-9.05

a replacement is accepted only when an answer of the previous round names the replaced requirement or criterion as contradictory or impossible, the round's amendments list records task, from, to and that answer number, and the next round judges it; a scope glob added is accepted only when an added criterion of that round reads a path under it, recorded with the answer number; the never-weakens check accepts exactly these and nothing else
staleness is judged at the signing commit for a contract already signed, and at HEAD for a spec not yet signed, so a signed contract's own landed work never makes it stale

criteria.statement: Each refusal rule is exercised by a fixture that is SIGNABLE until exactly one field is broken, and the broken fixture is refused with that rule's reason
A spec edited after its clean round is NOT SIGNABLE until a new clean round
A clean verdict with a non-empty answers list, and a round with answers left pending, are both refused
The gate script carries its version line

For every refused fixture and for a spec with no record, spawning `node scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs <spec>` (no --report) exits non-zero. Running `sh -c 'node scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs <spec> && echo PROCEED'` prints no PROCEED. For the SIGNABLE base fixture the exit is 0 and PROCEED is printed. Naming two specs where only one is SIGNABLE also exits non-zero.

The test pins one fixture spec's spec_sha256 to a literal hex constant. It also asserts the gate's hash equals canonicalHash({...spec, workdir: null}) from vendor/attest/signature.mjs, imported independently of the script. Changing only tasks[0].criteria[0].verifier.cmd, only a scope glob, or only interior whitespace in a statement makes the fixture NOT SIGNABLE with a hash-mismatch reason. Reordering keys or reformatting whitespace between tokens keeps it SIGNABLE. If record.spec_file names a different file whose hash matches the round, but the spec path passed on the command line differs, the result is NOT SIGNABLE.

Each of the following is applied as the only change between snapshot r1 and r2, with r2 a clean round whose hash matches the spec on disk: a grep pattern changed, a grep file changed, a test_red_green test_file changed, expect_exit changed or removed, mandatory:false added, a statement rewritten, a stop_rule removed, a requirement removed, a depends_on entry removed, or workdir set to a non-null path. Each is NOT SIGNABLE with a weakening reason naming the task and criterion statement. Swapping two criteria within a task is not reported as a removal.

Refused: a record where any round's snapshot is missing. Refused: a record where a snapshot's canonical hash differs from its round's spec_sha256. Each gets a reason naming the round. The case where r1.spec.json is overwritten with the current spec, so that a real weakening would disappear, is refused.

Each of these two-round records is NOT SIGNABLE with a reason naming round 1 and the answer number: round 2 clean with empty answers and a matching hash, while round 1 has one answer that is (a) pending, (b) missing its disposition, (c) rejected with reason '   ', or (d) added with no criterion object. The same record with round 1 fully dispositioned is SIGNABLE.

A command change between r1 and r2 is SIGNABLE only when round 2's amendments list has an entry with the same task, the same criterion statement, from equal to the r1 cmd and to equal to the r2 cmd. Refused cases: an amendment naming a different criterion, an amendment whose to differs from the r2 cmd, one amendment covering two changed commands, and an amendments list in a round other than the one whose snapshot holds the change.

In a temporary git repository: a clean round lists src/a.mjs with the sha256 of its first committed version, and a second commit changes it. The result is NOT SIGNABLE naming src/a.mjs, even after the working-tree copy is restored to the first version. The same holds when the path is written ./src/a.mjs, and when src/a.mjs is deleted at HEAD. A changed docs/x.md input is reported but stays SIGNABLE. A record whose clean round has inputs.files: [] while the spec's scope names a src/ path is refused.

The gate exports RULES, an array of reason codes. The test asserts it equals this literal list: schema, spec_id, rounds_contiguous, last_clean, last_empty, hash, dispositions_all_rounds, added_verbatim, rejected_reason, never_weakens, red_green_required, head_stale_src. The test asserts the base fixture is SIGNABLE. For every code there is a one-field mutation of that base that is refused with exactly that code and no other. The red_green_required fixture is refused when the manifest row is missing or says kind feature, and is SIGNABLE only when the manifest row says docs or evidence. A kind field inside the spec alone does not exempt it.

An answer with disposition added is refused when the spec on disk has a criterion with the same task, statement and verifier type but whose verifier is not deep-equal, under canonical JSON, to the answer's proposed verifier. The cases are: a different cmd, a different test_file, and a different grep pattern. An exact deep-equal match is SIGNABLE.

With no arguments, cwd set to a temporary tree that has one NOT SIGNABLE spec only under contracts/quality-loop/specs/, the gate prints that spec's line and exits non-zero. It does the same with the spec only under contracts/seed-readiness/specs/. Given a nonexistent spec path, or no specs found by default, it exits non-zero with a message saying so.

Independent of the test file's content: copy the committed base fixture test/fixtures/redteam/base/ (spec contracts/quality-loop/specs/QL-0.01.json, record contracts/quality-loop/redteam/QL-0.01.json) into a fresh temporary git repository for each case and run the real gate there, capturing stdout and stderr. Base: exit 0. One statement edited: non-zero, and the output names hash. Record deleted: non-zero, and NO RECORD is printed. Last round given one answer: non-zero. Last round's spec_sha256 replaced: non-zero. A gate that always exits 0, or always refuses, fails this check.

verifier.cmd: R=$PWD; G=$R/scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs; S=contracts/quality-loop/specs/QL-0.01.json; F=contracts/quality-loop/redteam/QL-0.01.json; fresh(){ T=$(mktemp -d) && cp -R $R/test/fixtures/redteam/base/. $T && cd $T && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t.invalid commit -qm b || exit 8; }; mut(){ node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),[f,js]=process.argv.slice(1),o=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8"));new Function("o",js)(o);fs.writeFileSync(f,JSON.stringify(o))' "$1" "$2" || exit 9; }; fresh; node $G $S || exit 1; fresh; mut $S 'o.tasks[0].criteria[0].statement+=" x"'; node $G $S >o.txt 2>&1 && exit 2; grep -q hash o.txt || exit 3; fresh; rm $F || exit 9; node $G $S >o.txt 2>&1 && exit 4; grep -q 'NO RECORD' o.txt || exit 5; fresh; mut $F 'o.rounds[o.rounds.length-1].answers=[{n:1,disposition:"rejected",reason:"x"}]'; node $G $S && exit 6; fresh; mut $F 'o.rounds[o.rounds.length-1].spec_sha256="0".repeat(64)'; node $G $S && exit 7; exit 0

criteria.statement: Each round carries sig, a DSSE envelope from vendor/attest/signature.mjs sign() over canonical({...round without sig, snapshot_sha256, previous round in full with its dispositions and amendments}). The signing key's keyid must be in the gate's REVIEWER_KEYS and must not be a key under contracts/keys/. The RULES literal list in the existing RULES criterion gains review_sig (otherwise the two criteria cannot both pass). Refused with review_sig: (a) a single clean round with no sig; (b) a round signed by the contract-signing key; (c) r1.spec.json and rounds[0].spec_sha256 rewritten together after r2 was signed; (d) a round-1 disposition or a round-2 amendment edited after the next round was signed. A correctly signed chain, made with test keys under test/fixtures/redteam/, is SIGNABLE.

A fixture whose spec on disk differs from the clean round's snapshot only by workdir '/tmp/elsewhere' is NOT SIGNABLE with never_weakens naming workdir, although canonicalHash({...spec, workdir:null}) still equals the round's spec_sha256. The same spec with workdir null is SIGNABLE. (A workdir the operator needs belongs on the runbook command line, not in the spec.)

Each is the only change between snapshot r1 and r2, with r2 clean and matching the disk, and each is NOT SIGNABLE with never_weakens naming the task (and the criterion, where there is one): scope glob broadened to '**'; scope glob added; verifier type test_red_green to command with the same cmd; metric value 0.9 to 0.5 under '>='; metric op '<' to '<='; metric key changed; task T2 deleted; the last criterion of T1 deleted; test_red_green cmd changed with no amendment; timeout_s 300 to 3000; grep flags 'i' added; phase implement to verify; a requirement reworded.

An added answer whose matching spec criterion carries mandatory:false, or any key other than statement, verifier, id and mandatory:true, is refused with added_verbatim. Any criterion that first appears in a snapshot with mandatory:false is refused with never_weakens. The same criterion without the extra key, or with mandatory:true, is SIGNABLE.

red_green_required is evaluated on the tasks as makeTask/contractDraft would draft them, and counts only mandatory test_red_green criteria. The clean round records manifest_kind, which must equal the manifest row when the gate runs. Refused with red_green_required: (a) a task with no phase key and only grep criteria; (b) a task whose only test_red_green has mandatory:false; (c) a clean round recorded with manifest_kind feature while the manifest row now says docs. The same spec with one mandatory test_red_green per task is SIGNABLE.

The clean round names the reviewed commit. In a temporary git repository with the spec's scope ['src/**', 'scripts/x.mjs'] and inputs.files ['src/a.mjs'], a second commit makes the pre-sign gate run refuse with head_stale_src when (1) src/b.mjs, unlisted but in scope, changed; (2) src/new.mjs was added; (3) scripts/x.mjs, in scope but outside src/, changed. A change only to docs/x.md, outside the scope, stays SIGNABLE and is reported. This applies to the plain (pre-sign) run only; for an already-signed contract, --report evaluates staleness at the signing commit (see answer 10).

In a temporary tree, --report exits non-zero and names the file when contracts/signed/k-xyz-abc123.json matches no spec by title or drafted tasks and its canonicalHash is not in the gate's GRANDFATHERED list. A copy of the real contracts/signed/k-memory-quality-multiling-4468b8.json in a temporary tree with both spec directories empty exits 0 (its hash is in GRANDFATHERED); the same copy with one character of its title changed exits non-zero as an orphan. --report also exits non-zero on a record that is not JSON, and on a record whose last round is clean but whose hash does not match.

In a temporary git repository: a clean round lists src/x.mjs; contracts/signed/k-xyz-abc123.json (tasks equal to makeTask of the spec) is added and committed; a later commit changes src/x.mjs. --report exits 0, because for a signed contract it evaluates head_stale_src at the commit that added contracts/signed/<id>.json (git log --diff-filter=A). The plain run on the spec is still NOT SIGNABLE with head_stale_src. If src/x.mjs changed before the signing commit, --report exits non-zero.

An added answer whose criterion names test_file test/new.test.mjs outside its task's scope is SIGNABLE when the next snapshot adds exactly that path (no glob) to the scope and that round's amendments list holds {task, scope_add: 'test/new.test.mjs', answer: '<round>.<n>'}. The same scope addition without that entry, or adding 'test/**' instead, is refused with never_weakens.
A spec or snapshot whose raw text has a duplicate key at any depth (a verifier with cmd twice) is NOT SIGNABLE with schema, although its parsed canonical hash equals the round's spec_sha256.
Changes stay in scope

stop_rules: If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.

tasks.title: Wired into the suite and documented
requirements: test/redteam-gate.test.mjs also runs the gate in --report mode over the repository's own spec directories, so npm test and CI fail on a malformed record or a signed contract without a SIGNABLE record, while NO RECORD is reported and not failed
docs/CONTRACTS.md gains a section that states the rule, the record path, the hash definition and the one-line runbook: gate, then memev contract new, then memev contract sign, in one command

memev contract new refuses a spec the gate reports NOT SIGNABLE or NO RECORD when the workdir holds scripts/gate/redteam-gate.mjs, naming the reasons; memev contract sign and the MCP sign tool refuse a draft whose source spec hash has no clean signed record; a repository without the gate script is unaffected

criteria.statement: A signed contract whose spec has no SIGNABLE record fails the suite's report run; a spec with no record does not
The contracts page states the rule

verifier.pattern: No contract is signed without a clean red-team record

criteria.statement: In a temporary repository tree, --report exits non-zero when contracts/signed/k-xyz-abc123.json (a real engine-shaped id) is linked to a spec by title, or by the tasks makeTask would draft from it, and that spec has no SIGNABLE record. It also exits non-zero when the signed contract's tasks differ from the spec's drafted tasks (one criterion cmd changed), and exits 0 when the record is SIGNABLE and the tasks match. The run over the real repository asserts the number of specs it examined, printed by the gate, equals the number of files in the two default directories. When those directories are missing it prints that fact instead of a bare exit 0.

The test pulls the single runbook line out of the fenced block in docs/CONTRACTS.md's red-team section and runs it with sh. PATH holds a stub memev that logs its arguments and prints a draft JSON with an id. On a NOT SIGNABLE fixture spec the stub is never called. On a SIGNABLE fixture it is called with 'contract new <spec>' and then 'contract sign <the id the stub printed>', with no hand-typed id. The same section must contain contracts/<area>/redteam/<id>.json and the hash definition (sorted keys, no whitespace, workdir null).

Scope widened to src/cli/contracts-cli.mjs and test/contracts.test.mjs (an existing file, so the red half is real). For a spec inside a contracts/<area>/specs/ tree, `memev contract new <spec>` runs the gate first. When the gate says NOT SIGNABLE or NO RECORD, the command exits non-zero and no file appears under the vault's contracts/drafts/. When it says SIGNABLE, the draft is created and records provenance.spec_sha256. `memev contract sign <id>` refuses a draft carrying provenance.spec_sha256 whose tasks differ from makeTask applied to that spec.
Changes stay in scope

stop_rules: If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
